_comment: Speed budgets. 'target' is the goal from the release plan; 'guard' is the
regression limit CI enforces today (measured baseline plus headroom).
A metric over its guard fails CI. Over target but within guard is reported
as tracked until the work that brings it in lands, then the guard drops to
the target. Never raise a guard to make CI pass: lower it when you improve
a metric, and explain any increase in the PR.
where: mac = macOS CI runner (release build, signed app); linux-webkit = CI WebKit.
Guards set 2026-10-11 from the first CI run, ~1.3-1.5x the measurement:
update_100kb 17.9, update_1mb 227.6, warm_open 1239, cold_start 5060,
write_to_update 423, web_first_apply_1mb 1351, web_update_20 197, long frames 417/600.
Revised 2026-10-11 after repeat runs showed run-to-run noise on shared runners:
warm_open 1239 and 1730 -> guard 2600; web_first_apply_1mb 1351 and 2096 -> 3000;
web_update_20 now includes the layout it causes: 225 and 459 ms in two runs -> guard 700;
scroll frame pacing in headless WebKit varied 417-528 long frames of 600 with no code
change, so scroll metrics are reported, not gated (guard null).
The macOS runner varies as much: update_100kb 17.9 and 26.6, update_1mb 227.6 and 355.7,
cold_start 5060 and 6462, write_to_update 423 and 466 with no parser change, so those
guards are ~1.5x the highest run: 40, 530, 9700, 700.
Since the open timings end at the first presented frame (not the synchronous apply), runs
measured warm_open 2587 and cold_start 8502: guards 3900 and 12800 (1.5x).
write_to_update measured to the painted frame: 936 ms (496 to the apply in the same
kind of run; the runner's display paces frames slowly) -> guard 1400.
Incremental parsing (M5): update_100kb 12.7 ms, update_1mb 66.1 ms on the macOS runner;
guards lowered to 20 and 100 (1.5x).
Word-level comparison (M6) runs inside the update for each edited block (word_diff_100kb
1.2-2.5 ms for the 20 edits). Eight macOS runs of the M6 branch measured update_100kb
12.1-25.9 ms and update_1mb 55.6-112.9 ms (the M5 runs: 11.0-16.9 and 59.2-91.2), with
no parser change between the fastest and slowest; a Linux release build measured the
same before and after the last M6 commits. Guards raised to 30 and 150 so runner noise
does not fail CI; targets unchanged.
3.2: update_100kb and update_1mb are measured on the fastest of 9 / 7 runs (runner
interference only adds time). Three macOS runs of the same commit: update_100kb 11.2,
11.7, 11.7 ms; update_1mb 59.0, 56.6, 51.9 ms. Guards lowered to 18 and 90 (1.5x the
highest); both now meet their targets.
3.4: update_1mb_minstr is the same update counted in instructions (millions) by valgrind
in the Linux core job (Packages/ReadoutCore/Tools/perf-instructions.sh), which runner noise
does not move. 3.3.0 measured 842 with Swift 6.1 on Linux; 3.4 (byte scans, parallel fragment
parsing) 395. Target: half of 3.3.0. Guard 1.3x the 3.4 measurement.
With those changes two macOS runs measured update_100kb 5.7 and 5.1 ms, update_1mb 25.4 and
23.4 ms (3.3.0: 12.0-12.7 and 64.6-78.6): guards lowered to 12 and 50 (about 2x the higher,
since parallel parsing on a shared runner may vary more); targets unchanged.
3.4 (web): web_update_20_blocks_1mb_ms now waits two frames after the scroll before the
update, so the scroll's own layout is no longer counted, and the update measures the blocks
it changed once after its ops instead of once per op (one layout instead of 20). Three CI
runs: 18, 21, 16 ms (3.3 on the old harness: 131-245 ms). Guard 700 -> 40: about 2x the
highest, since shared-runner runs of one commit have differed 2x (225 and 459 above).
web_first_apply_1mb_painted_ms (new): first apply until the frame showing it is painted;
three CI runs 3288, 2406, 1934 ms -> guard 4900 (1.5x the highest). web_first_apply_1mb_ms
measured 2361, 1610, 1266 in the same runs (unchanged code; 1017-2201 before): guard stays 3000.
